title: "FCS Enrichment - `r params$project_name`"
subtitle: "`r if (exists('params') && !is.null(params$traitname)) paste0('Trait: ', params$traitname) else if (exists('params') && !is.null(params$trait)) paste0('Trait: ', params$trait) else if (exists('params') && !is.null(params$project_name)) paste0('Project: ', params$project_name) else ''`"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%d %B %Y')`"
author: "PhyloPhere pipeline"
output:
  html_document:
    theme: flatly
    syntax_highlighting: tango
    toc: true
    toc_float:
      collapsed: false
    code_folding: hide
    df_print: paged
    fig_width: 10
    fig_height: 6
    self_contained: true
    mathjax: null                       # no math in this report
    md_extensions: "-tex_math_dollars"  # gene-set names contain '$' (e.g. V$HNF4_01) - never parse as TeX math
params:
  stats_file:   NULL          # TSV: gene + one-or-more score_<ranking> cols + optional flag_<name> cols
  universe_file: NULL         # cleaned_background (one gene symbol per line)
  gmt_dir:      NULL          # directory of curated *.gmt files
  project_name: "FCS"
  num_g:        10            # min genes per set (fastwilcoxGMT num.g)
  max_g:        0             # max genes per set (0 / Inf = no limit)
  fdr_thr:      0.15          # BH threshold on the permulation p of each set (q.perm), per ranking and database
  pperm_thr:    0.025         # raw permulation-p threshold of the Redlich rule
  gene_stat: "size_adj_max"      # gene statistic of the observed gene scores; the CAAS null must hold the same one
  score_source: "caas"       # pipeline source: caas (zero floor) or rer (exclude missing statistics)
  analytic_levels: "0.05,0.1,0.15" # analytic rule (Redlich et al. 2024): BH levels of the analytic p, with p.perm < pperm_thr
  cluster_similarity: "jaccard" # redundancy reduction: leading-edge similarity, jaccard or overlap
  cluster_threshold:  0.5     # redundancy reduction: similarity at which a set joins a representative
  top_n:        20            # rows shown per database x ranking
  leading_edge_top_n: 100     # rows shown in the pooled (all-database) leading-edge
                              # composition table, deliberately more generous than
                              # top_n, which caps a single database's slice, not the
                              # whole significant set for a ranking. A term that IS
                              # significant but ranks outside this cap will silently
                              # disappear from the on-page table (though never from
                              # fcs_results/fcs_leading_edge.tsv, which is unbounded).
  traitname:    "trait"
  perms_file:   "NO_FILE"
  enrich_file:  NULL          # pre-computed, GMT-batch-merged fcs_run_all() output (see fcs_compute.R /
                              # FCS_COMPUTE_BATCHED+FCS_CONCAT in fcs.nf). When NULL, falls back to running
                              # fcs_run_all() here directly (unbatched path, e.g. ad-hoc/manual rendering)
  annot_file:   "NO_FILE"     # optional cross-module annotation overlay (SCORING fcs_stats.tsv):
                              # supplies flag_* + CAAS score_top/score_bottom for the leading edge.
                              # When NO_FILE, annotation falls back to the stats file itself.
  gene_lists_dir: NULL        # SCORING's published gene_lists/slice_<dir><pct>.tsv dir, when
                              # supplied, gene percentile membership is read from there instead of
                              # re-ranking score_top/score_bottom here. ONLY pass this for the CAAS
                              # report (SCORING_FCS_REPORT), never for RER's (RER_FCS_REPORT),
                              # whose score_top/score_bottom are RER's own ranking, not CAAS's.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7, dev = "png", dpi = 200)

# ── Dependencies ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(knitr)
  library(kableExtra)
  library(patchwork)
})

# ── Theme and helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.title.y  = element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(l = 20, r = 20)),
    axis.title.x  = element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 12)),
    axis.text.x   = element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 5)),
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 6)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", hjust = 0, margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 10)),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.box.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 5)
  )
)
# Pin the dplyr verbs so that loaded packages cannot mask them.
filter <- dplyr::filter; select <- dplyr::select; rename <- dplyr::rename
mutate <- dplyr::mutate; arrange <- dplyr::arrange
# Fallback operator: b when a is NULL, empty or an empty string.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (!is.null(a) && length(a) > 0 && nzchar(as.character(a)[1])) a else b

# Load the shared FCS core (fcs_enrich.R). The process copies local/* into the work
# directory, so src/ sits next to this file; the other candidates cover manual renders.
this_dir <- tryCatch(dirname(normalizePath(knitr::current_input(), mustWork = FALSE)),
                     error = function(e) ".")
src_candidates <- c(file.path(this_dir, "src", "fcs_enrich.R"), "src/fcs_enrich.R", file.path(this_dir, "fcs_enrich.R"), "fcs_enrich.R")
src <- src_candidates[file.exists(src_candidates)][1]
if (is.na(src)) stop("fcs_enrich.R not found under src/ or next to FCS_general.Rmd")
suppressMessages(invisible(capture.output(source(src))))
src_cluster <- file.path(dirname(src), "fcs_cluster.R")
if (!file.exists(src_cluster)) stop("fcs_cluster.R not found next to fcs_enrich.R")
source(src_cluster)

# HTML table with the report style; optional scroll box of fixed height.
kbl_html <- function(df, height = NULL, escape = TRUE, caption = NULL, ...) {
  k <- kable(df, format = "html", escape = escape, caption = caption, ...) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(height)) k <- scroll_box(k, height = height)
  k
}
```

```{r load, include=FALSE}
# ── Inputs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
stopifnot(!is.null(params$stats_file), file.exists(params$stats_file))
stopifnot(!is.null(params$universe_file), file.exists(params$universe_file))

stats <- readr::read_tsv(params$stats_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
if (!"gene" %in% names(stats)) {
  gcol <- intersect(c("Gene", "GENE"), names(stats))[1]
  if (!is.na(gcol)) stats <- dplyr::rename(stats, gene = !!gcol)
}
stopifnot("gene" %in% names(stats))

# Universe: the cleaned background (all tested genes). It falls back to the scored genes
# when no valid background is given (for instance a NO_* sentinel file).
universe <- character(0)
if (!is.null(params$universe_file) && file.exists(params$universe_file) &&
    !grepl("^NO_", basename(params$universe_file))) {
  universe <- unique(trimws(readLines(params$universe_file)))
  universe <- universe[nzchar(universe)]
}
if (length(universe) < 2) {
  message("No valid universe file - falling back to scored genes as the universe.")
  universe <- unique(stats$gene)
}

score_cols <- grep("^score_", names(stats), value = TRUE)
if (length(score_cols) == 0) stop("stats_file has no score_<ranking> columns")
ranking_names_raw <- sub("^score_", "", score_cols)
# Canonical tab order: global, top, bottom. The column order of stats_file is incidental and
# must not drive it; a ranking outside this set is appended at the end in file order.
RANKING_ORDER <- c("global", "top", "bottom")
ranking_names <- c(intersect(RANKING_ORDER, ranking_names_raw),
                   setdiff(ranking_names_raw, RANKING_ORDER))

# Annotation overlay: the cross-module leading-edge flags (and the CAAS directional
# scores behind the top/bottom percentiles) come from a separate file when one is given
# (the fcs_stats.tsv of the CAAS report). A report ranked by its own score, such as the
# RER one, is then annotated with the CAAS, FADE and accumulation flags of each gene.
# Rankings always come from `stats`, annotation from `annot`; without an overlay `annot`
# is `stats` itself (the CAAS report carries its own flags).
annot <- stats
if (!is.null(params$annot_file) && file.exists(params$annot_file) &&
    !grepl("^NO_", basename(params$annot_file))) {
  annot <- readr::read_tsv(params$annot_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  if (!"gene" %in% names(annot)) {
    gcol <- intersect(c("Gene", "GENE"), names(annot))[1]
    if (!is.na(gcol)) annot <- dplyr::rename(annot, gene = !!gcol)
  }
}
flag_cols <- grep("^flag_", names(annot), value = TRUE)

# GMT directory: the parameter, else the dat/ directory of the module.
gmt_dir <- if (!is.null(params$gmt_dir) && nzchar(params$gmt_dir)) params$gmt_dir else file.path(this_dir, "..", "dat")
invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(gmts <- fcs_load_gmts(gmt_dir))))
desc_map <- suppressMessages(fcs_load_descriptions(gmt_dir))
```

# Overview

```{r overview, echo=FALSE}
tibble::tibble(
  Field = c("Project", "Trait", "Genes (stats)", "Background genes", "Rankings",
            "Flags", "GMT databases", "num.g (min set)", "max.g (max set)", "Significance rules"),
  Value = c(params$project_name, params$traitname, nrow(stats), length(universe),
            paste(ranking_names, collapse = ", "),
            if (length(flag_cols)) paste(sub("^flag_", "", flag_cols), collapse = ", ") else "(none)",
            length(gmts), params$num_g,
            ifelse(is.null(params$max_g) || params$max_g <= 0 || !is.finite(params$max_g), "(none)", as.character(params$max_g)),
            sprintf("RER: q.perm < %s; Redlich: analytic levels %s and p.perm < %s", params$fdr_thr, params$analytic_levels, params$pperm_thr))
) %>% kbl_html()
```

# Methods

Every gene set of every GMT database is tested against each ranking with the
**Wilcoxon-AUC test** (`RERconverge::fastwilcoxGMTall`), a rank-sum test that asks
whether the genes of the set sit systematically higher in the ranking than the other
genes of the universe. Its statistic, the **AUC** (`stat + 0.5`, range 0 to 1), is the
probability that a random gene of the set outranks a random gene outside it; 0.5 means
no shift. On a ranking where most genes score 0 the analytic p accounts for the ties
(the variance of the rank sum carries the tie term). RER is tested two-sided,
regardless of the observed signs; a set can be enriched on either side. Other rankings
use a two-sided test when they contain negative values, and a one-sided test otherwise.

For RER, genes without an association statistic are excluded from the observed
ranking; measured zero statistics remain. Missing null statistics are excluded
separately within each permulation. CAAS uses the tested background, filling genes
without a score with zero. Each GMT database restricts its background to annotated genes.

The analytic p (`p.adj`, BH within the database) assumes independent genes and species.
The decision rests on the **permulation p** (`p.perm`) instead: the same test is run on
every column of a null built by reassigning the phenotype across species on the real
tree, and `p.perm` is the fraction of null columns at least as extreme as the observed
one, with a pseudo-count. The compared statistic is `AUC - 0.5`: CAAS magnitude
rankings use the upper tail (`stat_null >= stat_observed`), targeting concentration
among genes with stronger convergence evidence. Signed RER rankings use both tails
(`abs(stat_null) >= abs(stat_observed)`). Both use `(1 + count) / (1 + valid cycles)`.
The analytic p is a separate column and is not the permulated quantity. Sets need
at least three annotated background genes outside the set on each side of the calculation.

* **RER rule** (`sig_perm`): `q.perm` below `r params$fdr_thr`, where `q.perm` is
  the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment of `p.perm` within each ranking and database.
* A ranking without a permulation null has no `p.perm` and so no significant set.

**Analytic rule (Redlich et al. 2024).** The rule published with RERconverge calls a set
enriched when its analytic BH-adjusted p (`p.adj`) is below a level and its permulation
p is below `r params$pperm_thr`, the permulation p being used as a filter and not corrected
for multiple testing. It is reported next to the rule above as `redlich_level`: the smallest of
the levels `r params$analytic_levels` that the set meets (empty when it meets none). It does not
enter `sig_perm` or the redundancy groups. Neither rule imposes a positive-statistic filter.

The sets are ordered everywhere by `q.perm`, then `p.perm`, then the size of the effect
(`|stat|`), then description.

**Redundancy reduction.** Gene sets of different databases, and parent and child terms
of one database, share genes. The significant sets of each ranking are grouped by the
similarity of their leading edges (`r params$cluster_similarity`, threshold
`r params$cluster_threshold`): the set with the smallest `q.perm` is a representative,
and each following set joins the first representative at least that similar to it, or
becomes a new representative (`cluster_id`, `is_representative`). The grouping is
applied after the significance call and changes no p or q value.

```{r run, include=FALSE}
# fcs_run_all() over every GMT database is the expensive step. The pipeline runs it as
# independent tasks, one per subset of GMT files (fcs_compute.R, FCS_COMPUTE_BATCHED in
# fcs.nf), and passes the row-concatenated result in enrich_file. The concatenation is
# exact because the BH correction is scoped per database (see fcs_compute.R). Without
# enrich_file (a manual render) fcs_run_all() runs here in a single pass.
if (!is.null(params$enrich_file) && nzchar(params$enrich_file) && file.exists(params$enrich_file)) {
  enrich <- readr::read_tsv(params$enrich_file, show_col_types = FALSE,
                             col_types = fcs_enrich_col_types())
} else {
  # One ranking vector per score_<ranking> column, with the source's missing-score policy.
  rankings <- list()
  for (sc in score_cols) {
    rk <- sub("^score_", "", sc)
    rankings[[rk]] <- fcs_build_vals(setNames(stats[[sc]], stats$gene), universe,
                                    score_source = params$score_source)
  }
  enrich <- suppressMessages(fcs_run_all(rankings, gmts, num_g = params$num_g,
                                         max_g        = params$max_g,
                                         perms_file   = params$perms_file,
                                         fdr_thr      = params$fdr_thr,
                                         p_perm_thr   = params$pperm_thr,
                                         analytic_levels = as.numeric(strsplit(params$analytic_levels, ",")[[1]]),
                                         gene_stat    = params$gene_stat,
                                         score_source = params$score_source))
}
enrich <- enrich %>% dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("sig_top"))
# Gene-set descriptions need the full GMT directory, so they are joined after the merge.
enrich <- enrich %>%
  dplyr::left_join(desc_map, by = c("database", "pathway")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(description = dplyr::coalesce(description, pathway))

# Per-gene attribute table: the annotation flags plus the derived directional percentile
# flags. They come from `annot`, so a per-module report inherits the CAAS, FADE and
# accumulation annotation.
pct_flags <- fcs_percentile_flags(annot, gene_lists_dir = params$gene_lists_dir)
attr_df <- pct_flags
if (length(flag_cols)) attr_df <- dplyr::left_join(pct_flags, annot[, c("gene", flag_cols)], by = "gene")
attr_cols_all <- setdiff(names(attr_df), "gene")

# A ranking with negative scores is signed (tested two-sided).
score_long <- stats %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, dplyr::all_of(score_cols)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "ranking", values_to = "drv_score") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ranking = sub("^score_", "", ranking))
ranking_signed <- vapply(split(score_long$drv_score, score_long$ranking),
                         function(v) params$score_source == "rer" || any(v < 0, na.rm = TRUE), logical(1))

# The leading edge keeps only the genes that drive each enrichment. In a magnitude ranking
# these are the members with signal (score > 0); gene.vals of fastwilcoxGMT lists every
# member in the universe, including zero-floored genes, and summarizing over those would
# dilute the composition with non-drivers. In a signed ranking they are the members whose
# score has the sign of the enrichment of the set (positive scores for a set enriched in
# the upper tail, negative for one enriched in the lower tail).
leading <- fcs_annotate_leading_edge(enrich, attr_df) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(score_long, by = c("gene", "ranking")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.signed = unname(ranking_signed[ranking])) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(drv_score) &
                  dplyr::if_else(.signed, drv_score != 0 & sign(drv_score) == sign(stat), drv_score > 0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-drv_score, -.signed)

# Redundancy reduction of the significant sets of each ranking (fcs_cluster.R).
enrich <- fcs_add_clusters(enrich, leading,
                           threshold = params$cluster_threshold, method = params$cluster_similarity) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sig = sig_perm %in% TRUE)
has_perm_any <- any(!is.na(enrich$p.perm))
n_sig <- sum(enrich$sig, na.rm = TRUE)

# Table order of the report: q.perm, p.perm, size of the effect, description.
ord_sig <- function(d) dplyr::arrange(d, q.perm, p.perm, dplyr::desc(abs(stat)), description)

dir.create("fcs_results", showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_tsv(enrich %>% select(-any_of("gene.vals")), "fcs_results/fcs_all_results.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(leading, "fcs_results/fcs_leading_edge.tsv")
```

```{r banner, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
n_rep   <- sum(enrich$is_representative %in% TRUE)
n_dbs   <- dplyr::n_distinct(enrich$database)
cat(sprintf(
  "**%d significant** gene sets by the RER rule (`q.perm` < %s), in **%d groups** of overlapping sets, across %d databases.\n\n",
  n_sig, params$fdr_thr, n_rep, n_dbs))
levels_chr <- strsplit(params$analytic_levels, ",")[[1]]
levels_num <- sort(as.numeric(trimws(levels_chr)))
cnt <- function(d, f) vapply(split(d, factor(d$ranking, levels = ranking_names)), f, integer(1))
rules_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Ranking = ranking_names,
  !!sprintf("RER: q.perm < %s", params$fdr_thr) := unname(cnt(enrich, function(x) sum(x$sig_perm %in% TRUE)))
)
for (L in levels_num) {
  rules_tbl[[sprintf("analytic p.adj < %s and p.perm < %s", L, params$pperm_thr)]] <-
    unname(cnt(enrich, function(x) sum(!is.na(x$redlich_level) & x$redlich_level <= L)))
}
cat("Sets called by each rule (the analytic ones are cumulative: a set at a smaller level also counts at the larger ones):\n\n")
print(kbl_html(rules_tbl))
cat("\n")
if (!has_perm_any) cat("_No permulation null was available: `p.perm` is empty and no set can be called significant._\n\n")
no_null_rk <- ranking_names[vapply(ranking_names, function(r) all(is.na(enrich$p.perm[enrich$ranking == r])), logical(1))]
if (has_perm_any && length(no_null_rk)) {
  cat(sprintf("_Rankings without a permulation null (no significant set): %s._\n\n", paste(no_null_rk, collapse = ", ")))
}
```

# Significant gene sets {.tabset .tabset-fade}

All sets with `q.perm` below the threshold, per ranking. `AUC` is the Wilcoxon effect size,
`p.adj` the analytic BH-adjusted p (reference only), `p.perm` the permulation p and `q.perm`
its BH adjustment.
`Group` is the redundancy group of the set and `Rep` marks its representative (the set of the
group with the smallest `q.perm`).

```{r significant_table, results='asis'}
for (rk in ranking_names) {
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n", rk))
  ev <- enrich %>%
    dplyr::filter(ranking == rk, sig) %>%
    ord_sig() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Description = stringr::str_trunc(description, 60),
      AUC         = round(stat + 0.5, 3),
      p.adj       = signif(p.adj, 3),
      p.perm      = signif(p.perm, 3),
      q.perm      = signif(q.perm, 3),
      Direction   = direction,
      Group       = cluster_id,
      Rep         = ifelse(dplyr::coalesce(is_representative, FALSE), "X", "")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(database, pathway, Description, num.genes, AUC, p.adj, p.perm, q.perm, Direction, Group, Rep)
  if (nrow(ev) == 0) { cat("_No set passed the significance threshold._\n"); next }
  print(kbl_html(ev, escape = TRUE, height = if (nrow(ev) > 15) "460px" else NULL))
}
```

# Analytic rule (Redlich et al. 2024) {.tabset .tabset-fade}

The sets that meet the analytic rule at the largest level of `r params$analytic_levels`, per ranking, in
order of level and then `p.adj`, capped at `r params$leading_edge_top_n %||% 100` rows. `Level` is the smallest
level met, `q.perm` and `Sig` tell whether the set is also significant by the permulation rule.

```{r redlich_table, results='asis'}
for (rk in ranking_names) {
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n", rk))
  rd <- enrich %>%
    dplyr::filter(ranking == rk, !is.na(redlich_level)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(redlich_level, p.adj, p.perm, description)
  n_rd <- nrow(rd)
  if (n_rd == 0) { cat("_No set meets the analytic rule._\n"); next }
  ltn <- params$leading_edge_top_n %||% 100
  if (n_rd > ltn) cat(sprintf("_Showing the first %d of %d sets; all are in `fcs_results/fcs_all_results.tsv` (`redlich_level`)._\n\n", ltn, n_rd))
  rd <- rd %>% head(ltn) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Description = stringr::str_trunc(description, 60), AUC = round(stat + 0.5, 3),
                  p.adj = signif(p.adj, 3), p.perm = signif(p.perm, 3), q.perm = signif(q.perm, 3),
                  Level = redlich_level, Sig = ifelse(dplyr::coalesce(sig_perm, FALSE), "X", "")) %>%
    dplyr::select(database, pathway, Description, num.genes, AUC, p.adj, p.perm, Level, q.perm, Sig)
  print(kbl_html(rd, height = if (nrow(rd) > 15) "460px" else NULL))
}
```

# Enriched gene sets {.tabset .tabset-fade}

The top `r params$top_n` enriched sets per database ordered by `q.perm` (a magnitude ranking shows
the sets with `stat` > 0, i.e. AUC > 0.5; a signed ranking shows both sides, with their direction),
whether or not they pass the thresholds.

```{r tables, results='asis'}
for (rk in ranking_names) {
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s {.tabset}\n", rk))
  sub <- enrich %>% filter(ranking == rk)
  if (!isTRUE(ranking_signed[[rk]])) sub <- sub %>% filter(stat > 0)
  if (nrow(sub) == 0) { cat("\n_No enriched sets._\n"); next }
  sub <- sub %>% ord_sig()
  db_sel <- sub %>% dplyr::group_by(database) %>% dplyr::slice_head(n = params$top_n) %>% dplyr::ungroup()

  for (db in unique(sub$database)) {
    disp <- db_sel %>% filter(database == db) %>%
      mutate(Description = stringr::str_trunc(description, 70),
             AUC     = round(stat + 0.5, 3),
             p.adj   = signif(p.adj, 3),
             p.perm  = signif(p.perm, 3),
             q.perm  = signif(q.perm, 3),
             Sig     = ifelse(dplyr::coalesce(sig_perm, FALSE), "X", ""),
             Direction = ifelse(stat > 0, "positive", "negative")) %>%
      select(pathway, Description, num.genes, AUC, p.adj, p.perm, q.perm, Sig, Direction)
    cat(sprintf("\n### %s\n\n", db))
    cat(sprintf("_%d shown - significant: %d._\n\n", nrow(disp), sum(disp$Sig == "X")))
    print(kbl_html(disp, height = if (nrow(disp) > 15) "420px" else NULL))
  }
}
```

# Overall dotplot {.tabset .tabset-fade}

One dotplot per ranking with its top `r params$top_n` significant sets, in the order of the tables
(`q.perm` first), on an axis of `-log10(q.perm)`; the dashed line is the BH threshold. Colour is the
AUC and size the number of genes of the set. Only the representative of each group of
overlapping sets is drawn, so a block of near-identical terms does not fill the plot.

```{r overall_dotplot, results='asis', fig.height=6}
# knitr opens the figure device once per chunk with the fig.height in effect at the
# start, so setting it inside the per-ranking loop does not resize the image written
# out. Each plot is rendered and embedded as a base64 PNG instead, which allows a
# different height per plot in one asis chunk.
.emit_sized_plot <- function(p, height_in, width_in = knitr::opts_chunk$get("fig.width"),
                              dpi = knitr::opts_chunk$get("dpi")) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  on.exit(unlink(f), add = TRUE)
  ggplot2::ggsave(f, plot = p, width = width_in, height = height_in, dpi = dpi, units = "in")
  cat(sprintf('<img src="data:image/png;base64,%s" style="max-width:100%%;" />\n\n',
              base64enc::base64encode(f)))
}

for (rk in ranking_names) {
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n", tools::toTitleCase(rk)))
  dp <- enrich %>%
    filter(ranking == rk, sig, is_representative %in% TRUE) %>%
    ord_sig() %>%
    head(params$top_n) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(label = stringr::str_trunc(dplyr::coalesce(description, pathway), 55),
                  signal = -log10(pmax(q.perm, 1e-300)))
  if (nrow(dp) == 0) { cat("_No significant sets for this ranking._\n\n"); next }
  # y index 1 is the bottom of the plot: reversing the order puts the best term at the top.
  term_levels <- rev(make.unique(dp$label))
  dp$label <- make.unique(dp$label)
  dp <- dp %>% dplyr::mutate(y = as.numeric(factor(label, levels = term_levels)))

  p <- ggplot(dp, aes(x = signal, y = y)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = signal, yend = y), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(size = num.genes, colour = stat + 0.5)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(params$fdr_thr), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(term_levels), labels = term_levels) +
    scale_colour_gradient2(name = "AUC", low = "#2166ac", mid = "#d9d9d9", high = "#b2182b",
                           midpoint = 0.5, limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "set genes") +
    labs(title = sprintf("%s - %s", params$project_name, rk),
         x = expression(-log[10]~q[perm]), y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black", size = pmax(8, pmin(11, 220 / length(term_levels)))),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal")
  .emit_sized_plot(p, height_in = pmax(4, pmin(22, 2.2 + 0.35 * length(term_levels))))
}
```

# Leading-edge composition {.tabset .tabset-fade}

For each significant set (`q.perm` < `r params$fdr_thr`), the **percentage of its leading-edge
genes** carrying each attribute: directional score percentiles and cross-module support. Sets are
ordered as in the tables above (`q.perm` first) and capped at `r params$leading_edge_top_n %||% 100`
rows; if a ranking has more significant sets than that, the table says so explicitly rather than
silently dropping the low-ranked ones. `Group` and `Rep` give the redundancy group of the set and
whether it is the representative.

```{r leadingedge, results='asis'}
# Display names of the attribute columns.
disp_names <- c(
  pct_top25 = "top25%", pct_top10 = "top10%", pct_top5 = "top5%", pct_top1 = "top1%",
  pct_bottom25 = "bot25%", pct_bottom10 = "bot10%", pct_bottom5 = "bot5%", pct_bottom1 = "bot1%",
  flag_fade = "fade", flag_fade_top = "fade_top", flag_fade_bottom = "fade_bottom",
  flag_rer_acc = "rer_acc", flag_rer_decc = "rer_decc",
  flag_accum = "accum", flag_accum_top = "accum_top", flag_accum_bottom = "accum_bottom"
)
# Attribute columns shown per ranking (direction-aware). flag_accum is the
# non-directional accumulation test; flag_accum_top and flag_accum_bottom are its
# direction-restricted versions, as flag_fade, flag_fade_top and flag_fade_bottom are
# for FADE. The pct_* tiers are the top 25, 10, 5 and 1% of the genes with a score above 0
# in the score_top (pct_top*) and score_bottom (pct_bottom*) rankings of `annot`.
cols_by_rk <- list(
  global = c("pct_top25","pct_top10","pct_top5","pct_top1",
             "pct_bottom25","pct_bottom10","pct_bottom5","pct_bottom1",
             "flag_fade","flag_rer_acc","flag_rer_decc","flag_accum"),
  top    = c("pct_top25","pct_top10","pct_top5","pct_top1",
             "flag_fade_top","flag_rer_acc","flag_rer_decc","flag_accum_top"),
  bottom = c("pct_bottom25","pct_bottom10","pct_bottom5","pct_bottom1",
             "flag_fade_bottom","flag_rer_acc","flag_rer_decc","flag_accum_bottom")
)

le_comp_all <- list()  # leading-edge composition tables, exported after the loop

for (rk in ranking_names) {
  cat(sprintf("\n## %s\n\n", rk))
  want <- cols_by_rk[[rk]] %||% attr_cols_all

  sig_terms_rk <- enrich %>% filter(ranking == rk, sig)
  if (nrow(sig_terms_rk) == 0) { cat("_No sets passed the significance thresholds for this ranking._\n"); next }

  le_rk_all <- leading %>% filter(ranking == rk) %>%
    semi_join(sig_terms_rk, by = c("ranking", "database", "pathway"))
  if (nrow(le_rk_all) == 0) { cat("_No sets passed the significance thresholds for this ranking._\n"); next }

  # Order by the report convention over every significant term before cutting the table,
  # so the rank of a term does not depend on the cut. It is the order of the tables above.
  ltn <- params$leading_edge_top_n %||% 100
  n_sig_rk <- nrow(sig_terms_rk)
  term_order <- sig_terms_rk %>%
    ord_sig() %>%
    head(ltn) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.rank = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::select(database, pathway, .rank)

  le_rk <- le_rk_all %>% semi_join(term_order, by = c("database", "pathway"))

  if (n_sig_rk > ltn) {
    cat(sprintf("_Showing the top %d of %d significant sets for this ranking (order above); the rest are truncated here but remain in `fcs_results/fcs_leading_edge.tsv` (unbounded) and, if within a database's own top %d, in the Enriched gene sets tables above._\n\n",
                ltn, n_sig_rk, params$top_n))
  }

  summ <- fcs_leading_edge_summary(le_rk, want) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(term_order, by = c("database", "pathway")) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(.rank) %>%
    dplyr::select(-.rank) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(sig_terms_rk %>% dplyr::select(database, pathway, q.perm, cluster_id, is_representative),
                     by = c("database", "pathway")) %>%
    left_join(desc_map, by = c("database", "pathway")) %>%
    mutate(Description = stringr::str_trunc(coalesce(description, pathway), 50),
           q.perm      = signif(q.perm, 3),
           Group       = cluster_id,
           Rep         = ifelse(dplyr::coalesce(is_representative, FALSE), "X", "")) %>%
    select(database, pathway, Description, n_le, q.perm, Group, Rep,
           any_of(intersect(want, names(.))))
  # Rename the attribute columns to their display names.
  present_attr <- intersect(want, names(summ))
  names(summ)[match(present_attr, names(summ))] <- disp_names[present_attr]
  print(kbl_html(summ, height = if (nrow(summ) > 15) "480px" else NULL))

  # Keep the table for export, with a ranking column.
  le_comp_all[[rk]] <- summ %>% dplyr::mutate(ranking = rk, .before = 1)
}

# Export the leading-edge composition of all rankings (read by 15.Comparison_report.Rmd).
le_comp_export <- dplyr::bind_rows(le_comp_all)
if (nrow(le_comp_export) > 0) {
  readr::write_tsv(le_comp_export, "fcs_results/fcs_leading_edge_composition.tsv")
}
```

# Method

```{r method, echo=FALSE}
cat("Test       : Wilcoxon-AUC (RERconverge::fastwilcoxGMTall); RER always 'two.sided'; other rankings 'greater' unless they contain negative scores\n")
cat("Null       : AUC - 0.5 per null column; upper tail for magnitude rankings, absolute statistic for signed rankings; pseudo-count (1 + n) / (N + 1)\n")
cat("RER rule   : q.perm < ", params$fdr_thr, " (BH on p.perm per ranking and database)\n", sep = "")
if (params$score_source == "rer") {
  cat("Universe   : genes with a non-missing RER statistic; measured zeros retained; null NA excluded per permulation\n")
} else {
  cat("Universe   : cleaned_background; no-signal genes floored to 0 (zero-floor)\n")
}
cat("Groups     : greedy by significance, leading-edge ", params$cluster_similarity, " >= ", params$cluster_threshold, " to a representative\n", sep = "")
cat("Analytic   : p.adj < level and p.perm < ", params$pperm_thr, ", levels ", params$analytic_levels, " (Redlich et al. 2024; redlich_level)\n", sep = "")
cat("Order      : q.perm, p.perm, |stat|, description\n")
```

tested with the Wilcoxon-AUC test and called significant on the BH-adjusted
permulation p as described in Methods above. `r n_sig` set(s) are significant.
